items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: And he arranged a beautiful version of “Monk’s Mood” on the “Album Album.” At the time I was using an electric melodica so I could add another voice to the arrangement.

ctx.x: Um hum. I’ll run a few names by you and just wonder if you have a comment or association that you might share with me. One would be Howard Johnson.

Yeah well Howard was a unique musician in the sense that he played tuba and saxophone and played trumpet. And he was a good composer/arranger. And he arranged a beautiful version of “Monk’s Mood” on the “Album Album.” At the time I was using an electric melodica so I could add another voice to the arrangement. It was really great. A very talented guy.
I was just listening to that this morning and your “New Orleans Strut” that you wrote I think for your father is very hooky. Really sticks in your head.

items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Yeah… Then I added Howard Johnson.

ctx.x: So you had a three (horn) frontline then?
Yeah… Then I added Howard Johnson.
